evidence: Both manifest exports select bundled ESM/CJS React UI components; the archive also includes the corresponding source, styles, documentation and tests. There are no package scripts or installation hooks. Registry tarball bytes match the supplied archive exactly.

Uploader handles a user-selected/dropped file list, validates/parses CSV or Excel, and calls a beforeUpload callback. Only when an action prop is supplied does it append accepted files to FormData and POST them through serverApi or fetch(action). No fixed attacker endpoint or credential source is supplied.

DataTable stores visibility/table configuration under formName in localStorage. Clipboard reads are in a paste callback gated by editable selected cells; copy handlers serialize the selected table data. These are editing operations, not a clipboard monitor or credential collector.

Papaparse XMLHttpRequest logic streams a caller-supplied CSV URL and optionally posts a caller-supplied request body. downloadjs converts data URLs to Blobs and triggers save/open UI. JSZip/pako and write-excel-file construct spreadsheet XML and ZIP output for export.

mathExpressionEvaluator.eval in NumericInput follows lex -> toPostfix -> postfixEval arithmetic evaluation. Function("return this")() is Lodash global-object discovery, and new Function in setImmediate is the standard bundled callback adapter. Neither consumes a recovered external payload in the supplied application paths.

Fuse createIndex builds an in-memory search index, startsWith("https") classifies an example-file download URL, and Lodash checks coreJsData.keys.IE_PROTO to recognize masked native functions. Those concrete benign paths refute the old database/import/core-js claims.
